reconstructed_captions.26: A hand uses small snips to cut the threads after finishing the seam.
reconstructed_captions.27: The sewn black leather pieces are laid out on the workbench.
reconstructed_captions.28: A hand applies leather cement along the edge of one of the leather pieces.
reconstructed_captions.29: The two leather pieces are carefully aligned and pressed together.
reconstructed_captions.30: A hand uses a mallet to tap along the seam, ensuring a strong bond.
reconstructed_captions.31: A stitching groover tool is used to carve a shallow channel for the stitches.
reconstructed_captions.32: A hand uses a pricking iron and a mallet to punch stitching holes along the groove.
reconstructed_captions.33: A close-up shows the evenly spaced, diamond-shaped holes in the leather.
reconstructed_captions.34: The leather piece is secured in a wooden stitching pony for hand sewing.
reconstructed_captions.35: A hand begins saddle stitching the leather using two needles and waxed thread.
reconstructed_captions.36: A close-up view shows the needles passing through the holes in opposite directions.
reconstructed_captions.37: The stitching continues along the edge of the leather piece.
reconstructed_captions.38: The final stitches are made and backstitched to secure the thread.
reconstructed_captions.39: The excess thread is trimmed close to the leather with a sharp blade.
reconstructed_captions.40: A hand uses an awl to mark the position for a snap fastener.
reconstructed_captions.41: A circular hole punch is placed on the mark and struck with a mallet.
reconstructed_captions.42: A clean hole is created in the leather for the snap.
reconstructed_captions.43: A hand inserts the post of the snap component through the hole in the leather.
